g.text: 10,000 troops arriving per day by spring 1918 -at a time when Germany was unable to replace lossesKey role in Peace Offensive [March -July 1918] preventing advance on Paris 1.2 million committed by time of Spring OffensivePlayed key role in allied final counter-offensive: Hundred Days offensive August -November. Second Battle of the Marne fought between July 18 and August 6. The Allies, bolstered by significant numbers of Americans, halted the German offensive.Battle of the St. Mihiel Salient fought from September 12 to September 16, 1918; over half a million US troops participated. Meuse-Argonne offensive, was launched on September 26, with British, French, and American forces attacking the Germans on a broad front. Meuse-Argonne campaign cost 2550 US lives a day. 26 000 in 6 weeks.By end of war Allies could field 600,000 more troops than GermanyIn November 1918, US had co-ordinated infantry-artillery supported by aerial bombardment which led to advancesUS etered war late. Bulk of US fighting only in last 6 monthsTook over a year to deploy armyOnly lost 53,500 in combat -no comparison to 20 000 lost 1stday of SommeAnglo-French forces had already:*Held the Marne in 1914*Held Verdun in 1916*Inflicted huge casualties on German forces*Overstretched the German army -Italian Front 1915 [Russian offensive 1916]*Modernised strategy / use of tanks at Cambrai 1917*By Spring 1918 Allies have worn German army down*French led the counter-offensive in 1918* British navy had successfully bloacked Germany and broken the u-boat campaign
Impact of US entry on the western front
Role of British and French forces on the western front
